correctness.rationale: Exact compound-Poisson exponential cumulants yield a positive two-atom moment law for orders three to six. The first three node moments admit an exhaustive one-parameter positive support-and-weight representation. Explicit positive derivatives show the true admissible parameter range is one open interval, proving the strict five-cumulant feasibility criterion and the exact range of clock variance. An exact decreasing sixth-cumulant formula gives the sharp compatibility ray and unique constructive inverse. All boundaries and strict positivity are specified; 729 exact-rational parameter checks and an explicit five-moment alias test were executed independently of the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The specific sharp *physical feasibility and partial-identification* theorem—strict five-cumulant existence inequalities, complete clock-noise variance interval and exact sixth-cumulant lower ray—was not located in the consulted historical hydrological studies or the relevant research-record searches. The transport process, Gaussian higher-cumulant cancellation, and Prony inversion are acknowledged as established. The assessed novelty is their nontrivial joint admissibility and extremal result; a possible broader moment-theoretic implication remains an explicit risk, so priority is provisional.
residual_risks: Classical truncated Stieltjes moment or Markov–Krein extremal theory may imply the exact admissible interval by specialization; historical priority provisional.
The primary-paper text was accessible in substantive excerpts but no complete original publisher PDF was exhaustively checked.
Prony recovery and Gaussian cumulant cancellation are established tools, not claims of novelty.
High-order cumulant estimates can be unstable under finite-sample noise or long tracer tails.

value.rationale: River tracer storage experiments use temporal summaries, while storage heterogeneity and timing uncertainty confound identification. The exact sharp five-cumulant clock-variance interval, explicit realizability inequalities and strict sixth-cumulant lower bound give operationally meaningful finite-moment constraints beyond computing an individual model solution. A rare-but-very-slow storage class drives the unbounded sixth-moment edge without disrupting five fixed cumulants. The theory does not assert statistical robustness.
